answer: Each identity must lock a slashable bond before its work counts, cut like an opal from one rough stone: dividing it among fake shards only multiplies the capital at risk. Standing grows slowly, willow-like, across graded epochs, and a proven link between accounts sends a ripple of slashing through the whole cluster. A sybil farmer must fund and season a separate bond for every fake, so one exposed link burns them all, while an honest agent pays only once.
